package_info.package_versions: Unknown (latest version at time of report)
package_info.why_malicious: DEFENSOR ID is a banking Trojan distributed via the official Google Play Store. It masquerades as a legitimate security or banking tool but is designed to steal sensitive information from victims, including bank account credentials, cryptocurrency wallet private keys, and two-factor authentication codes. The app abuses Android permissions and accessibility services to harvest credentials and exfiltrate them to a remote command-and-control server, violating user trust and platform policies.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, after app launch and upon user granting permissions
execution_context.file_location: Main application code (Android app, likely in MainActivity or a persistent background service)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after the user launches the app and grants permissions, the code abuses accessibility services to monitor user input, captures banking credentials and two-factor authentication codes, searches device storage for cryptocurrency wallet private keys, and exfiltrates all collected data to a remote command-and-control server, resulting in theft of sensitive financial information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code requests and abuses sensitive permissions such as accessibility services, SMS access, and file system access to monitor user input, intercept SMS messages, and search for private keys. It then exfiltrates this sensitive data to an external server, which is not required for any legitimate app functionality.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate banking or security app should never capture user credentials through accessibility services, intercept SMS 2FA codes, or search for private keys in device storage. Nor should it transmit such sensitive data to external servers without explicit user consent and secure handling.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Accessibility services may be legitimately used by apps to assist users with disabilities, and SMS access may be used for auto-filling verification codes, but these should not be used to harvest credentials or exfiltrate sensitive data.
key_indicators: Abuse of BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE to monitor and capture user input
Interception of SMS messages via READ_SMS for 2FA code theft
Unusual file system access patterns targeting known wallet file locations
Outbound network communication to remote C2 infrastructure
Exfiltration of credentials and private keys in unencrypted HTTP POST requests

attack_chain.action: User installs DEFENSOR ID from the Google Play Store and grants requested permissions, including accessibility, SMS, and storage access.
attack_chain.leads_to: App is launched and is able to access sensitive device features.

attack_chain.action: App abuses accessibility services to monitor user input and capture credentials for banking and financial apps.
attack_chain.leads_to: User credentials are harvested from input fields.

attack_chain.action: App intercepts incoming SMS messages to steal two-factor authentication codes.
attack_chain.leads_to: 2FA codes are harvested, enabling bypass of additional security measures.

attack_chain.action: App searches device storage for cryptocurrency wallet private keys and other sensitive files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Wallet keys and sensitive files are harvested from device storage.

attack_chain.action: All harvested credentials, 2FA codes, and wallet keys are exfiltrated to a remote command-and-control server controlled by the attacker.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive user data, enabling account takeover and financial theft (final goal).

behavioral_signatures: Abuse of Android accessibility services (BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE) to monitor and capture user input in other apps
Interception of SMS messages via READ_SMS permission for 2FA code theft
Unusual file system access patterns targeting directories and filenames associated with cryptocurrency wallets (e.g., searching for wallet.dat, keystore files)
Exfiltration of sensitive data (credentials, 2FA codes, wallet keys) to external servers via unencrypted HTTP POST requests
file_indicators: AndroidManifest.xml requesting BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE, READ_SMS, READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, and INTERNET permissions
App package name and signing certificate not matching those of legitimate banking or security apps
Presence of code or resources referencing known banking app package names or wallet file paths
network_indicators: Outbound connections to domains or IP addresses associated with known banking trojan C2 infrastructure
Unencrypted HTTP POST requests containing credential or wallet data to external servers
Network traffic to hardcoded or dynamically resolved C2 endpoints not associated with legitimate app functionality
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Android apps requesting excessive or sensitive permissions (especially BIND_ACCESSIBILITY_SERVICE, READ_SMS, and storage access). Use static analysis to identify code patterns that monitor user input, intercept SMS, or search for wallet files. Employ dynamic analysis to observe runtime credential harvesting and exfiltration behaviors. Inspect network traffic for unencrypted POST requests containing sensitive data to suspicious domains or IPs. Flag apps whose package name or certificate does not match known legitimate vendors, and correlate with behavioral indicators for automated detection.
